newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher on active foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher on active foreign buying.

text.p: Stocks closed higher on Saturday, buoyed by aggressive buying from foreign investors betting the strength of the Japanse yen would boost South Korean exports, brokers said.
They said improved investor sentiment would continue to prop up shares next week.
The composite stock index stood at 706.25 at the close, up 6.72 points from Friday. Advancing issues outpaced decliners by 557 to 217.
The impending arrest of President Kim Young-sam's son has largely been ignored, brokers said.
"The strength of the yen continued to help lift market sentiment," said Rho Chang-yeoul of Samsung Securities.
While foreign buying focused on low-priced large cap issues, most local investors favoured small- to mid-sized stocks, brokers said.
Foreign investors continued to show interest in Daewoo shares because of their low prices, they said.
Daewoo Electronics closed at a limit high of 14,900 won, up 1,100, while Daewoo Heavy Industries rose 210 won to 6,900.
